care_team_notes: Ask the MND advisor, GP, psychologist, counsellor or clinic team about emotional support early, especially after diagnosis, major function changes, communication changes or carer strain.
description: MND-specific guidance on emotional distress, adjustment, fear, anxiety, anger, sadness, isolation, relationships and everyday mental wellbeing strategies.
name: Emotional wellbeing with MND

care_team_notes: Screen and review cognition/behaviour with GP, neurologist, MND clinic and clinical neuropsychology; check whether changes could also relate to mood, fatigue, sleep, medicines or communication difficulty.
description: MND-specific information about changes in thinking, behaviour, personality, language, decision-making, motivation, emotional expression and daily planning.
name: Cognition, thinking and behaviour in MND

care_team_notes: If MND/FTD is suspected, plan early for supported decision-making, legal/advance care planning, routine simplification, behaviour support, carer education and safety.
description: Information about frontotemporal dementia and the MND/FTD overlap, including behaviour, personality, language, movement, progressive support needs and family impact.
name: MND and frontotemporal dementia

care_team_notes: Explain emotional lability to family and paid carers; ask the GP/neurologist/MND clinic about management if episodes are distressing, misunderstood or affecting relationships.
description: MND information about emotional lability or pseudobulbar affect, where crying or laughing may not match how the person feels.
name: Emotional lability and pseudobulbar affect

care_team_notes: Ask the GP or mental health professional for review when worry, panic, low mood, hopelessness, sleep disturbance, withdrawal or irritability are affecting daily life.
description: Australian guidance about anxiety, depression, symptoms, self-care, psychological therapy, medicines, online supports and when to seek professional help.
name: Anxiety and depression support

care_team_notes: Check whether distress is related to diagnosis, loss of independence, relationship changes, communication difficulty, financial pressure, carer load or future planning.
description: General Australian guidance on grief, stress, loss, coping, practical support and when extra help may be needed.
name: Grief, stress and adjustment

care_team_notes: For immediate danger, use emergency services; for non-immediate distress, connect with GP, mental health services, MND association, Lifeline, Beyond Blue or other appropriate supports.
description: Australian mental health support pathways for urgent distress, immediate risk, counselling, crisis support and finding professional help.
name: Urgent mental health support pathways
publisher: Healthdirect Australia / Lifeline Australia / Beyond Blue
